summary: PlymHealth: bulk session-resume fanout latency spike causing missed streaming frames and SLA exposure
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~13:50 UTC PlymHealth began reporting a widespread increase in latency and frequent streaming frame drops for batched 'session-resume' fanout requests. Impact: customer-facing chat features experienced truncated or delayed responses, and PlymHealth's SLA dashboard recorded >15% of requests exceeding the 1s p50 latency SLO during the window. Environment: production, us-east-1, heavy batched fanout path for session-resume, primarily traffic to redwood-13b-v2.

Timeline / Observed behavior: 1) 2026-03-10 13:48 UTC - first alert from internal latency dashboard (route: /v1/chat/stream) showing p95 jump from 600ms to 2.8s. 2) 13:50 UTC - PlymHealth support rep posts to #support and opens a high-priority ticket. 3) 13:55 UTC - increased 5xx rate (502/504) on streaming gateway correlating with large fanout batches from PlymHealth customer-id. 4) 14:05 UTC - mitigation attempted (rate-limit backoff configuration and temporary reduction of max_batch_size for the customer), partial improvement but intermittent frame drops continued. 5) 14:40 UTC - fallback routing to smaller model variant (redwood-7b-quant) enabled for a subset of sessions to reduce tail latency; customer escalated to enterprise success for credits and root-cause.

Steps to reproduce (internal): 1) Simulate batched session-resume requests with fanout_count >= 40 and sequence lengths > 512 tokens. 2) Observe queue depth on serving-runtime and streaming-gateway metrics (queue_length, kv_cache_miss_rate). 3) Reproduce elevated kernel-selection stalls under quantized execution path.

Immediate impact metrics: - P50 latency increased from 0.58s to 1.2s for affected route. - P95 latency spiked to ~2.8s. - Streaming frame incomplete ratio rose from 0.3% baseline to 6.4% during window. - Approximate customer error budget burn: 22% for the 1-hour window.

Current mitigation in place: - Temporary per-customer batching cap set to 8 for PlymHealth at the router layer. - Canary fallback to redwood-7b-quant for 30% of sessions (gradual). - Enabled additional streaming-gateway logging for PlymHealth session_ids and request_ids.

Customer ask: PlymHealth requests a timeline, root-cause analysis, and a credit for SLA exposure. They also asked for a durable configuration option to cap fanout per-tenant to avoid recurrence.

Desired next steps: 1) Confirm root cause (kernel/kernel-selection interactions under high fanout and long sequences, possible KV-cache eviction amplification). 2) Implement a short-term scheduler patch to prioritize session-resume small-batches and reduce preemption of streaming workers. 3) Post-incident: propose a tenant-level fanout guard and documented operational runbook. 4) Draft customer-facing postmortem and propose billing credit calculation.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:10 UTC - SRE (Rafael) hypothesis: long-sequence fanout pushes KV cache churn, causing repeated cold-cache misses and kernel-selection thrash on quantized path; leads to blocking on GPU worker and streaming timeouts.
Heap/metrics snapshot: worker_queue_depth correlated with p95 latency spikes; kernel selection latency in traces increased by 3.5x for affected requests.
Checked autoscaler events: no scale-up events coincident with first spike (autoscaler throttled due to cooldown settings) - potential capacity constraint during fanout window.
Routing logs show PlymHealth traffic had unusually large batch_size values (40-60) coming from an SDK integration they rolled out at 13:30 UTC.
Initial reproduction: lab test with synthetic fanout 48x + sequence 1024 tokens reproduced the p95 increase and streaming frame truncation in staging with the same quantized kernel config.
Related: PR #2441 contains earlier kernel-selection logic changes for quantized models; flagged for review as potential contributor.
No evidence of authentication or network-level errors; 5xx appears service-side (worker queue / memory pressure).

2026-03-10 14:30 - Lina Chen (Runtime Eng): Observed increased kernel fallback rate to slower execution path for quantized models; reproducing locally with synthetic load. Creating draft PR for quick fix to reduce KV eviction under fanout.
2026-03-10 15:05 - Customer Success (Marta Ruiz): Informed PlymHealth of temporary mitigations and ETA for root-cause analysis; customer requested SLA credit estimate and formal postmortem.
2026-03-11 09:20 - Rafael Gomez (SRE): Follow-up: running extended soak tests overnight with patched batching scheduler; early signs show p95 reduction but still under validation.

resolution_notes: Workaround: enforced per-tenant max_batch_size at router and temporary fallback routing to smaller model for a subset of sessions reduced immediate SLA burn.

Short-term fix (merged to canary 2026-03-11): scheduler patch to yield on high kv-cache-miss-rate and prioritize streaming-critical worker slots (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2478).

Planned long-term actions: 1) tenant-level fanout limiter feature in router (spec + implementation owner: Lina Chen). 2) Revise autoscaler cooldown logic to allow emergency transient scale-up for streaming-critical routes. 3) Add a targeted regression test harness for fanout+long-sequence scenarios.
Customer remediation: proposing pro-rated SLA credit for the affected 1.5 hour window; awaiting finance approval and final calculation.
Follow-up items created: INT-? (internal task to track router limiter implementation) and a public postmortem page under OPS.

Monitor PlymHealth traffic for 72 hours after full rollout of scheduler patch; report metrics daily to customer.
